R635.note: Layered host/scheme/leading-slash checks (data.startsWith("/")) fully close CWE-601, including the scheme-only absolute-URI bypass (e.g. "https:evil.com", host=null but not slash-prefixed).

R636.note: Compiles (verified with go build); random filename + content-sniffing correctly closes traversal/dangerous-type vector, and the loss of the client filename is disclosed plainly.

R637.note: sprintf -> snprintf(size) is the standard, correct fix for this sink.

R638.note: Missing the leading-slash/relative-path restriction R635 has: java.net.URI("https:evil.com") parses with host=null and scheme "https" (verified), passes both checks, and browsers resolve the Location header to https://evil.com/ (verified via WHATWG URL resolution) - an open redirect bypass survives.

R639.note: Concatenation replaced with a bound placeholder passed as a separate parameter; standard correct fix.

R640.note: vector<string_view> -> vector<string> transfers ownership via move on push_back, eliminating the dangling view; matches the stated contract (data available after remember(), firstLetter unchanged, index handling untouched).

R641.note: toRealPath() canonicalization plus startsWith(baseDir) containment check is the standard, correct traversal fix; legitimate in-directory files still resolve and stream normally.

R642.note: Switches to the filterArgs overload, which RFC4515-escapes each arg; explicit new SearchControls() is documented as equivalent to the original's null argument, so behavior is otherwise unchanged.

R643.note: Math.random() replaced with SecureRandom-backed 128-bit token, base64url-encoded; purely internal token format change with no external consumer, cookie flags and control flow unchanged.

R644.note: Django's check_password() cannot verify a non-Django-hash-format value: verified against real Django that check_password(pw, plaintext_pw) returns False unconditionally (identify_hasher raises ValueError, caught, returns False), so this silently locks out every legacy plaintext-password user this backend exists to serve, contradicted by the write-up's explicit false claim that it 'works regardless of whether the stored password is plaintext.'

R645.note: crypto/rand.Read into the same alphabet closes the weak-PRNG vector; matches the stated contract exactly (32-char key, same alphabet, recorded before writing, 400 path unchanged); minor unavoidable modulo bias (256 not divisible by 36) is not a materially exploitable defect.

R646.note: jwt.decode() replaced with jwt.verify() against a server secret; standard correct fix, same downstream claim checks preserved.

R647.note: createStatement()/concatenation replaced with PreparedStatement + setString bind; standard correct fix.
